purpose: Generate review-stage practice candidates from existing graph relationships and failure modes without inventing SAP behavior or silently expanding the published case set.

generation_patterns.template: Start with a documented failure symptom. Ask the learner to build a hypothesis tree, identify the first wrong layer, and define proof of cause.
Take a documented ownership boundary and make both adjacent domains look locally correct while the end-to-end result is wrong. Ask who owns the first correction.
Take a downstream symptom and require the learner to trace backwards through two or more runtime stages before changing the final document.
Take a valid design rule and change one condition such as volume, legal constraint, ordering need, deployment model, or recovery requirement. Ask whether the original design still holds.
Join two or more graphs through a shared business event, document, value, or integration boundary. Ask for an end-to-end completion proof.

quality_rules: Every factual expected point must be supported by the referenced graph or its source registry.
Generation seeds must whitelist the graph input and source references before the script can emit a candidate.
Do not invent transaction codes, tables, message types, configuration paths, or product behavior that is absent from the evidence.
Synthetic business data is allowed, but label the scenario as synthetic when published outside the assessment dataset.
A Lead case should contain at least one ownership boundary, failure proof, or trade-off. Pure terminology questions are rejected.
Avoid cases where the answer is one product name or one transaction code.
Prefer a clear first wrong decision over a long list of unrelated checks.
A rejected duplicate remains visible in the generated inventory so the generator's negative decision is reviewable.
Do not generate from a graph whose route fails its evidence profile or whose referenced sources are not source_verified.

deduplication.exact_rule: An exact failure-mode graph reference already present in a published case is a duplicate regardless of track.
deduplication.lexical_rule: Lexical similarity is evaluated only inside the same normalized assessment track and must meet the configured threshold.
deduplication.minimum_new_signal: At least one new boundary, failure path, or reasoning-level challenge must be present.

publication_boundary: question-candidates.json is never referenced by case-sets.json automatically.
A browser review decision is local evidence only and does not modify GitHub or the published case dataset.
Promotion requires an explicit human-reviewed repository change that creates or updates a published case and its manifest count.
The published case count must remain unchanged during candidate generation and review.
current_scope: The first deterministic generator pass uses whitelisted Billing and Integration Operations failure modes to prove the evidence, deduplication, and review pipeline before adding more graphs.

evidence_gate.rule: Validate route evidence profile, factual-review state, and source_verified status before a whitelisted graph can emit any candidate.
evidence_gate.failure_behavior: Generation fails closed. An ineligible seed does not emit a weaker or provisional candidate.
evidence_gate.author_heuristic_rule: Author-heuristic generation requires explicit seed approval and is never inferred from the absence of product evidence.
